title: Neutralizing Antibody Detection
author: Shihong Fu
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bdati2en

steps.title: Prepare Serum Dilutions
steps.instruction: Perform serial dilutions of the inactivated serum in a 96-well plate using MEM culture medium.

substeps.instruction: Mix 24 μl of inactivated serum with 96 μl of MEM culture medium to achieve an initial 5-fold dilution.
Serially dilute the serum two-fold from 1:5 to 1:160.

steps.title: Prepare Virus Dilution
steps.instruction: Dilute the virus using MEM culture medium to a concentration of 200 pfu/100 μl.

steps.title: Neutralize Virus with Serum
steps.instruction: Mix the diluted serum and virus and incubate to allow neutralization.

substeps.instruction: Mix equal volumes of the diluted serum (1:5 to 1:160) and 200 pfu of JE virus (strain P3).
Prepare virus controls at dilutions of 100 PFU, 10 PFU, and 1 PFU.
Incubate the mixture at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 1 h.

steps.title: Inoculate BHK-21 Cells
steps.instruction: Add the neutralized mixture to BHK-21 cells.

substeps.instruction: Use 6-well plates containing BHK-21 cells grown to 90% confluence in monolayer.
Inoculate the cells and incubate at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 1 h.

steps.title: Apply Overlay and Culture
steps.instruction: Apply a methylcellulose overlay and incubate until plaques are visible.

substeps.instruction: Supplement with 4 ml of 1.2% methylcellulose-MEM medium containing 2% FBS.
Culture at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 3-5 days until obvious viral plaques are observed.

steps.title: Stain and Calculate Neutralization
steps.instruction: Stain the cells to visualize and count viral plaques.

substeps.instruction: Stain with crystal violet for 1 h.
Gently rinse with running water and dry.
Count the number of viral plaques and calculate the neutralizing antibody of JE virus in the sample.
